extracted.intended_audience: general readers; students and scholars of 19th-century American history and legal remedies for kidnapped free persons
extracted.subtask_description: An excerpt from Solomon Northup's memoir recounting his delivery from slavery, related legal proceedings, and appended statutory and memorial documents. The page mixes narrative, courtroom description, and statutory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governor's duty to restore kidnapped free citizens (§1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the Governor of this State shall receive information satisfactory to him that any free citizen or inhabitant has been kidnapped or transported out of the State for the purpose of being held in slavery, or is wrongfully seized, imprisoned or held in slavery on the pretence that such person is a slave, it shall be the duty of the Governor to take such measures as he shall deem necessary to procure such person to be restored to his liberty and returned to this State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Governor is authorized to appoint and employ agents, furnish credentials and instructions likely to accomplish restoration, and determine agents' compensation and necessary expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent powers and responsibilities (§1, §2)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agent appointed by the Governor shall be furnished with credentials and instructions and proceed to collect proper proof to establish the right of the person to freedom, perform such journeys, take such measures, and institute and prosecute legal proceedings as necessary under the Governor's direction to procure restoration and return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent may be appointed and employed as the Governor deems necessary; he shall gather proof, undertake travel and legal actions, and is to be guided and directed by the Governor's instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial accounting and advances for agent services (§3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts for all services and expenses incurred in carrying the act into effect shall be audited by the Comptroller and paid by the Treasurer on his warrant out of the State treasury; the Treasurer may advance reasonable sums on the Comptroller's warrant to enable the agent to accomplish his duties, for which the agent must account on final audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural financial safeguard: audit by Comptroller, payment by Treasurer, and provision for reasonable advances with subsequent accounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statute effective immediately (§4)
rubrics_metrics.description: This act shall take effect immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No delay in implementation; measures authorized by the statute may be employed at once.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recorder's certificate contents (example template)
rubrics_metrics.description: The recorder's certificate (sample text) certifies: the presenting person produced due evidence of the freedom of the named person; includes a physical description (age, height, hair, eyes), nativity (native born of State of New-York), and a request that civil authorities let the freed person pass unmolested, concluding with recorder's hand and seal and date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of a signed and sealed official certificate describing the person and attesting to freedom provides a pass and official imprimatur to protect transit; include identifying details and an explicit request to authorities to permit passage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of replevin to test right to freedom (procedural choice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal process in the nature of replevin may be issued, directed to the sheriff, commanding him to take the person into custody and detain until the decision of the court to test the question of right to freedom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers must be properly drawn and signed (Judge's signature required); timing considerations (e.g., night filings, judge availability) and prompt service can be critical to prevent concealment by opposing parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearsay and admissibility concerns in examination of witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements of third persons may be objected to as hearsay and deemed improper evidence (example: objection by counsel that 'sayings of third persons, being hearsay, was improper evidence').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearsay objections may be raised to exclude testimonial assertions not based on witness's direct knowledge; however, judges may overrule such objections depending on context and discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroboration via documentary evidence (bill of sale) and production of records
rubrics_metrics.description: When testimony asserts a bill of sale exists (to corroborate a purchase), prosecution may call for production of such a bill; examination of business records (sales books) can confirm or refute claimed transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to produce the alleged bill of sale or absence of an entry in sales records undermines the claim of a lawful purchase and can be decisive in assessing credibility of defendant's account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical practice: racial exclusion of testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: In the narrated proceedings, the court rejected the defendant's (Solomon's) own evidence on the ground that he was a colored man—demonstrating a practice of excluding or devaluing testimony by Black persons despite their status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This entry documents a prejudicial legal practice (admissibility/exclusion based on race) evident in the period; it is descriptive/historical rather than normative guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorial/petition format (Appendix B example)
rubrics_metrics.description: A memorial/petition to the Governor includes: petitioner's name, residence, maiden name (if applicable), age, date and place of marriage, and factual recital pleading the petitioner's case (as shown in the 'Memorial of Anne').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a formal declarative style including identifying personal details and relevant facts to present a petition to the Governor; follow customary headings and respectful address to the office.
